# Rome 46 BC – Scientific method & philosophical ideas

- **Scientific method (conjecture, test, publish, repeat)** [`scientific_method`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_method.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Greek books hold observation and some experiment (Strato, Archimedes, Alexandrian physicians). Romans prize utility and ancestral precedent; a public test reads as spectacle, not proof. Elsewhere: Alexandria, Museum.
- **Test claims instead of trusting authority** [`empiricism_over_authority`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/empiricism_over_authority.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Academic sceptics argue both sides and follow no master; Cicero says so openly. In medicine and farming, ancestral custom and famous Greek names still decide. Local: Cicero.
- **Controlled comparison (experiment with control group)** [`controlled_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/controlled_trial.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Owners of large slave households and army commanders could compare groups at will; nobody thinks to. A single cure or a votive tablet counts as proof. Local: large slave households (familiae); the legions.
- **Placebo effect and blinded trials** [`placebo_blinding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/placebo_blinding.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low
- **Correlation, causation and confounding** [`correlation_causation_confounding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/correlation_causation_confounding.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Greek logic names the fallacies and Carneades' objections to divination are known. Omens, dreams and remedies are still judged by remembered hits.
- **Selection and survivorship bias, fair sampling** [`selection_bias_sampling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selection_bias_sampling.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. The Diagoras retort about the votive tablets of sailors who did not drown circulates in Greek; Cicero retells it in 45 BC. Nobody applies it to remedies or omens.
- **Measurement and quantification** [`measurement_quantification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/measurement_quantification.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Standard weights, steelyards, surveyors' groma, sundials and water-clocks. Greek astronomy measures; natural philosophy argues in words. Roman numerals make tables clumsy. Local: Sosigenes, Caesar's calendar astronomer; land surveyors (mensores). Elsewhere: Alexandria and Rhodes, graduated instruments and star catalogues.
- **Nature follows simple mathematical laws** [`mathematical_laws_of_nature`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mathematical_laws_of_nature.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Archimedes on the lever and floating bodies, Pythagorean string ratios and Hipparchus are in Greek books. Romans treat mathematics as surveying and accounts. Elsewhere: Alexandria; Rhodes.
- **Falsifiability (risky, testable predictions)** [`falsifiability`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/falsifiability.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Refutation by counterexample is courtroom and school routine. Augural rules cannot fail: an omen that misleads means a flaw in the ritual.
- **Fallibilism (all knowledge of nature is provisional)** [`fallibilism_provisional_knowledge`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fallibilism_provisional_knowledge.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The sceptical Academy teaches that nothing is certain and one follows the probable. Cicero professes it; his Academica comes in 45 BC. Local: Cicero. Elsewhere: Athens, the philosophical schools.
- **Weighing evidence (base rates and Bayesian updating)** [`bayesian_reasoning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bayesian_reasoning.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Carneades' grades of plausibility are known through Cicero's teachers. No numbers attach to chance; dice are for gaming, lots for the gods.
- **Reproducibility and open publication** [`reproducibility_open_publication`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reproducibility_open_publication.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Books spread by private copying; Greek engineers published their catapult formulae. Craft recipes stay inside workshops and slave households. Disclosure earns no priority or reward. Local: T. Pomponius Atticus and his copyists.
- **Systematic errors of human judgement (cognitive biases)** [`cognitive_biases`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cognitive_biases.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Rhetoric teaches how to exploit them: appeals to fear, hope and party. Nobody treats them as errors to guard against in one's own judgement.
- **Formal logic (valid deduction and fallacies)** [`formal_logic`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/formal_logic.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept medium. Stoic and Aristotelian logic is taught by Greek tutors in great houses. Latin terms are still being coined; Cicero's Topica comes in 44 BC. Elsewhere: Athens; Rhodes.
- **Parsimony (Occam's razor)** [`occams_razor`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/occams_razor.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Epicureans do the opposite on principle: for things in the sky every explanation the senses do not contradict is kept (Lucretius V–VI).
- **Thought experiment** [`thought_experiment`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/thought_experiment.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Lucretius' spear thrown from the edge of the universe is in circulation; Zeno's paradoxes and Carneades' plank of two shipwrecked men are school pieces.
- **Source criticism (testing documents and reports)** [`source_criticism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/source_criticism.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Varro and Atticus (Liber annalis, c. 47 BC) sort chronology; Cicero's Brutus (46 BC) says family funeral speeches falsified history. Priestly records and prodigy lists go unquestioned. Local: Varro; Atticus; Cornelius Nepos.
- **Consent and ethics of experiments on people** [`informed_consent_research_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/informed_consent_research_ethics.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Greek physicians know the Hippocratic oath. Slaves have no say in their treatment and are tortured for evidence; condemned men are at the magistrate's disposal.
- **Natural causes (naturalism about disease, weather, comets)** [`natural_causes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_causes.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Lucretius and Greek meteorology explain thunder, eclipses and plague without gods. The state still expiates prodigies; one senator can hold both views. Local: Lucretius' De rerum natura (c. 55 BC); Varro; Cicero.
- **Scepticism towards astrology, omens, witchcraft and transmutation** [`scepticism_superstition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scepticism_superstition.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. Cicero is an augur and privately doubts divination (De divinatione, 44 BC). Auspices can stop an assembly, so augury is constitutional machinery. Astrology is a rising fashion. Local: college of augurs; Etruscan haruspices such as Spurinna; Cicero. Elsewhere: Babylon, omen astronomy and horoscopes.
- **Atomism (matter is made of tiny particles in motion)** [`atomism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atomism.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. Epicurean doctrine, widely read: Lucretius in Latin, Philodemus and Siro on the Bay of Naples. Opponents call it godless. Nobody can test it. Local: Lucretius' De rerum natura; Philodemus at Herculaneum; Siro at Naples; C. Cassius Longinus, recent Epicurean.
- **The same physical laws on earth and in the heavens** [`universal_physical_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_physical_laws.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Epicureans hold that sky and earth are the same atoms. Stoics and Aristotelians put a finer fire or aether above, and most people think the stars divine.
- **Mechanical philosophy (explain by matter and motion, not hidden purposes)** [`mechanical_philosophy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mechanical_philosophy.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Epicureans reject purposes in nature. Stoic providence is the respectable view and suits state religion. Greek machines and planetaria are admired as marvels. Local: Archimedes' geared planetarium from Syracuse, kept by Marcellus' family; his star globe stood in the temple of Virtus (Cicero, De re publica I). Elsewhere: Alexandria, the mechanics after Ctesibius; Rhodes.
- **Idea of progress (knowledge accumulates, the future can be better)** [`idea_of_progress`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/idea_of_progress.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Lucretius V tells how the arts advanced step by step, yet expects the world to decay. Romans measure by ancestors: 'new things' (res novae) means revolution.
- **Invention as a method (organised research and development)** [`systematic_invention`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/systematic_invention.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Alexandrian engineers found the catapult formula by royally funded trials; the account is in Greek. Rome pays contractors and generals' engineers, not research. Slaves are cheap. Local: Caesar's engineers (his praefecti fabrum Balbus and Mamurra; Vitruvius served on artillery). Elsewhere: Alexandria.
- **Golden rule and universal ethics** [`golden_rule_universal_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/golden_rule_universal_ethics.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Greek maxims and Stoic duties to all mankind are known; Cicero's De officiis comes late in 44 BC. In practice duty follows rank, kin, patron and client.
- **Human equality and dignity** [`human_equality_dignity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/human_equality_dignity.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Stoics teach that all men share reason and one world-city. Rank, citizenship and slavery order everything; yet freed slaves become citizens, which astonishes Greeks.
- **Natural (human) rights** [`natural_rights`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_rights.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Cicero's De re publica (51 BC) calls true law right reason in agreement with nature. Actual rights are a citizen's: appeal to the people, the tribune's help. Local: Cicero.
- **Social contract (government by consent)** [`social_contract`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_contract.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Epicureans call justice a compact not to harm; Lucretius V has men agree on magistrates and laws. Cicero defines the commonwealth as a people joined by agreement on law.
- **Freedom of thought, speech and the press** [`freedom_of_speech_thought`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/freedom_of_speech_thought.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Libertas includes frank speech in Senate and public meetings. Under Caesar men speak with care; Cicero's praise of Cato (46 BC) is answered by Caesar's Anticato, not by force.
- **Religious toleration and freedom of conscience** [`religious_tolerance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/religious_tolerance.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Foreign cults are admitted or suppressed by Senate decree (Bacchanalia 186 BC; Isis altars pulled down in the 50s). Caesar confirms the Jews' worship. Cult is civic duty, belief private.
- **Secular state (separation of religious and civil authority)** [`secular_state`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secular_state.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Priesthoods are public offices held by politicians: Caesar is pontifex maximus, Cicero an augur. There is no separate clergy to separate from.
- **Utilitarianism (judge rules by their consequences for everyone)** [`utilitarianism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/utilitarianism.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Epicurean reckoning of pleasure is for the individual, and Cicero attacks it (De finibus, 45 BC). 'Public advantage' is a familiar argument but means the citizen body.
- **Abolition of judicial torture; proportionate, certain punishment** [`abolition_of_torture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_torture.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Citizens are exempt from torture; a slave's testimony is valid only under it. Advocates such as Cicero call such evidence worthless when it hurts their client.
- **Positive-sum cooperation (trade is not zero-sum)** [`positive_sum_cooperation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/positive_sum_cooperation.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Wealth means land and plunder, and conquest visibly pays. Senators may not own large ships (law of 218 BC) and trade through freedmen and equites.
- **Game theory (prisoner's dilemma, credible commitment)** [`game_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/game_theory.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Caesar's clemency and his crossing of the Rubicon are commitment moves made by instinct. There are no words for it.
- **Commons problem and how communities solve it** [`tragedy_of_the_commons`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tragedy_of_the_commons.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Public land: legal limits on holdings and grazing were evaded by the rich, and the Gracchi died over it. Aqueduct water is tapped illegally.
